It falls short of client-ready because of the awkward cover CTA overlapping the house illustration, the repeated empty gap above the cards, small body text, and a weak final CTA with no contact route.

defects: Hook is weak: at 0.4s the frame is only a faint lilac blob with the brand line, no headline or flower, so the first second is nearly empty

The piece is held back by an empty, clipped opening, a title that is clipped again and then disappears, a poster that catches a broken mid-transition frame, and an end card with small text, no real call to action and dead space at the bottom, so it would need a fix pass before posting.

It loses points for cramped, fused title lettering, a tiny low-contrast footer and CTA, and a busy lower half, but it is close to postable.

It is not client-ready without a stronger hook, a cleaner layout and a fixed copy.

But the flat clip-art illustrations, awkward headline breaks, collisions between the footprint strip and the nav labels, and empty gaps on several slides keep it at solid template level rather than agency-ready.

defects: Hook frame (first second): headline 'Leurs vaccins, on y pense' is cropped mid-reveal, with the second line sliced in half, so the opening frame is a weak or broken thumbnail.
First frame: dog and cat illustration is cut off at the bottom edge and sits at a different size and position from the next beat, which reads as a jump.
Calendar scene: the card is pushed to the top and roughly the bottom third of the frame is empty, so the layout is unbalanced. The 'Réserver' headline is also clipped mid-reveal on one sampled frame.
Poster frame is the calendar scene with an empty lower third, so it does not sell the brand (no animals, no clinic name).

End card: dog and cat are cropped at the bottom, and in one frame only their heads show. The phone number and the SMS line start dimmed or tiny, and 'Rappel par SMS offert' is very small for a Stories viewer.

The main offer (free SMS reminder) only appears as a small pill and in the end card.
scores.verdict: A warm, coherent and reassuring piece in a cream, terracotta and green palette. It has a clear hook-to-booking narrative, correct French copy, and a working calendar and SMS demo that matches the brief. Framing and polish are inconsistent, though: the opening headline is clipped, the animals are cropped, the lower third is empty in the calendar scenes, and the small text is weak. It is postable after a fix of the first frame and the layout, but it is more solid template work than distinctive.

scores.verdict: A coherent, distinctive dot-matrix and film-strip system with clear numbered structure and correct English/UK copy, but the vertical dot-matrix words are hard to read and redundant, spacing is uneven, and decoration overshadows a fairly generic educational message. It is a solid template-level carousel that needs layout tightening and a stronger CTA and risk-warning treatment before posting.

defects: Composition is top-heavy in several beats: the SANS RDV / PREMIER ARRIVÉ block sits in the upper half and the lower ~55% of the frame is empty black.
The 'TOUS DESSINÉS MAIN' grid frame leaves the bottom third empty, and its two small cells (n°19 and n°39) look unfinished mid-draw. It also sits at the top with the 40 MOTIFS caption very small.

Micro text is far too small for a 1080x1920 phone screen: 'FLASH DAY — MARSEILLE', 'LE FLASH, DÈS' inside the red cell, '11H–20H · SAM. 14 NOVEMBRE', '40 FLASHS DÈS 60 € · SANS RDV', the address and the handle on the end card.
The end card puts the key practical info (date, hours, address, handle) in tiny mono type below a large logo, with no clear call to action such as 'Viens', and an empty lower third.
Frame 1: the dark-red '40' on a red halftone background has weak contrast, so the hero number reads mushy. The red blob behind the black '60€' is muddy and off-centre.

The flash motifs are generic thin-line clip-art icons (dagger, heart, skull, eye, bolt, rose) that look like UI icons rather than raw hand-drawn flash. This weakens the 'dessinés main' claim and the brief's photocopy and halftone aesthetic.
'60€' is written without the French narrow non-breaking space before the euro sign, and elsewhere it appears as '60 €', so the two are inconsistent.

Several beats appear held for two sampled frames with little visible motion, so pacing may feel less like 'cuts rapides' than the brief asks. The piece has only about 6 beats and no real tattoo imagery or people.
The logo lockup has 'TATTOO' in red offset and slightly misaligned below 'ENCRE NOIRE'.
scores.verdict: The palette (black, off-white, one red), the halftone, the grain and the condensed grotesque headlines fit the brief and the audience well, and the copy is clean, punchy French with all the key information. scores.verdict: This is a strong, coherent concept: a copper pressure gauge and pipe run through the whole deck, a needle that climbs through the signs, a tagline revealed one word per slide and an inverted cream offer slide. It suits a heritage family plumbing business in Nantes. The execution needs fixing before posting: the needle covers the numerals on every slide, one emoji is off-style, several titles leave an orphan word and the advice is generic, so it reads as a good draft rather than finished agency work.

scores.verdict: A coherent, distinctive copper-pressure-gauge concept with a good green, copper and cream palette, and the offer slide is clear with a strong CTA block. It falls short of client-ready because the needle covers the scale numerals, the low-contrast footer tagline and the dead space on slides 2-6 hurt legibility, the advice copy is thin and generic, and the slide 4 title is awkward.

Copy: 'DE PAUSE' as the label under '40 min' is odd and vague. The 'Baume apaisant' step (4) is not in the brief's list (serviette, blaireau, coupe-chou). Nothing conveys the neighbourhood (Croix-Rousse) or an old-school warmth beyond the small tag on the second hook frame.

The hook line 'On ne se rase pas. On se fait raser.' is a decent idea but generic. The price and duration card is too static, and the 35 € has no space before the euro sign (French convention needs a thin non-breaking space).
The step icons are generic line-art and inconsistent in weight and quality (the jar icon looks like a cosmetics pot, and the towel is ambiguous).
scores.verdict: The brand feel is right, with a barbershop palette of cream, oxblood and gold, refined serif and italic type, and a clear ritual structure that leads to price and CTA. Execution is only a decent template. Layouts are top-heavy with big empty bottoms, several sampled frames catch empty or half-built states, the icons are generic, and the end card is small and weak for a booking objective.

defects: '40 min DE PAUSE' is the wrong term: the 40 minutes is how long the treatment lasts, while 'temps de pause' means processing time or downtime. It should read 'de soin', 'de rituel' or 'en fauteuil'
Every ritual frame and the end card leave the bottom 30–35% of the 9:16 canvas empty, so the layout is top-heavy and the content stops well above the lower safe zone

Line-mask reveals leave half-cut lines of text on screen for a noticeable time ('rase pas.' at 0.3 s, 'Serviette chaude', 'Réservez', and the opening-hours line still unmasking at 19.8 s), so the end-card info is not fully readable until the very last moment
In transition frames the icons are empty or half-drawn: stray dashes in the step-04 medallion and the razor icon only partly drawn
The shaving-brush icon (with bubbles) and the balm-jar icon (a strange face-like label) look generic and a little clumsy next to the refined typography
The price card is empty for a beat while its frame draws on, so the key 35 € / 40 min information comes in late
No photo or human element: an all-vector explainer for a warm neighbourhood barber feels more like a template than a real shop
scores.verdict: This is a coherent, well-typeset old-school barber identity with a strong French hook ('On ne se rase pas. On se fait raser.'), a clear four-step ritual, and an end card with the price, address, hours and booking link. It is held back by the misused 'de pause', the empty lower third on almost every frame, slow mask reveals and generic icons, so it is solid professional work but not standout.

defects: Hairline seam artifact crossing the word 'jetable.' in the hook frame (~0.6s), from the text reveal mask

End-card CTA fades in from a very low-contrast state (visible in the sheet), and the CTA is a static bar with no strong action
The 'ÉTAPE 01/02/03' label sits far from the number and the two do not align cleanly. Title and number are separated by a large void
No visible barber or human element, no photography and no motion beyond fades, so the piece is generic and template-like
Dense hairline double frame and small uppercase labels near the edges risk being covered by the Reels/TikTok UI
scores.verdict: The dark-and-gold register suits an old-school Croix-Rousse barber, and the French copy is correct, with a decent hook ('Posez le rasoir jetable.') and a clear three-step structure that ends on the price and a CTA. It falls short of client-ready: the icons are ambiguous, the text is small, the lower part of the frame is empty, and there is a visible seam artifact on the hook and an awkward dash on the end card.

defects: The coupe-chou line illustration is crude. The open blade reads as a loop or spoon rather than a straight razor, and it is the weakest drawing in the set.
The step cards leave the bottom ~35% of the frame empty. All the content sits in the top two-thirds, so the layout feels top-heavy.
The step descriptions ('Elle ouvre les pores et détend la barbe.') are small, about 30px on 1080 width, so they are hard to read on a phone in a Reel.
At ~0.4s a faint horizontal hairline already crosses 'jetable' before the slice animation plays, a small artifact.
The slice mid-transition on 'jetable' (~2s) leaves the word briefly illegible while it overlaps itself. This is intentional, but the moment runs long.
End-card hours 'Mar. – sam. · 9h–19h' mix a spaced gold en dash with an unspaced one, which is inconsistent. French convention would be 'Mar.–sam.' or 'Du mardi au samedi'.
It is all text and line art, with no photo or footage of the salon, the chair or a real shave. The warm, human, neighbourhood feel in the brief comes through only through colour.
The CTA 'Réservez en ligne' appears only in the last ~2s. There is no earlier prompt to book.
scores.verdict: This is a coherent, tasteful premium-barber identity: a dark and gold palette, a strong serif, a clear 3-step ritual structure, and a complete end card with URL, address and hours, all in correct French. It is held back by a crude razor drawing, top-heavy layouts with small body copy, and a generic 'luxury template' feel that lacks the warmth and real human presence of a local Croix-Rousse shop.

defects: Hook: the headline 'On a ressorti' sits low and its second line 'le coupe-chou.' is not on screen during the first second (only a cropped gold 'le' fragment at 0.6s), so the hook reads as an unfinished sentence
Sheet frame 1 shows 'ressorti' clipped along its bottom edge by the reveal mask

The gold tracking on the tiny 'MAISON CASTEL — BARBIER' header is small, and the header repeats on every step frame
scores.verdict: A coherent, tasteful old-school barber identity (oxblood, gold and cream, serif italics, 40-minute dial as a structuring device) with correct French copy and a clear price and CTA end card. Its first-second hook is weak (cropped and incomplete headline), several transition frames are empty or mid-state, and the layouts sit high with dead space below, so it is solid but not best-in-class.

defects: The hero 'coupe-chou' is drawn like a table or pocket knife: blade and handle are in line, with black serrated notches on the spine. A barber would not recognise it as a straight razor, and it is the key prop of the whole piece.
The coupe-chou step icon inside the dial (frame 7) is just a hook-shaped curve with no clear meaning; it reads as a stray stroke.
Frame 3 is an empty, half-drawn dial with no text, which is dead time early in a 20 s Reel.

In almost every frame the bottom 35–40% of the screen is empty dark space. Content sits high and the layout feels top-heavy rather than intentionally placed around the platform UI.
The hook builds word by word ('On a…' at 0.4 s), so the full hook line is not readable until about 1 s.
The small-caps kicker 'MAISON CASTEL — BARBIER' and the step labels are small and low-contrast gold on brown; they are marginal at phone size.
The copy never says the soin is new ('nouveau') other than a tiny kicker. Online booking gets a single URL with no incentive or urgency.
The name of the neighbourhood (Croix-Rousse) appears only inside the circular seal text, not in legible copy, which weakens the local hook.
scores.verdict: This is a coherent, tasteful old-school barber identity: a 40-minute dial structures the four steps well, the serif/condensed type pairing is good, the French copy is clean and correct, and the end card is complete. It is held back by an inaccurate razor illustration (the hero prop reads as a table knife), several empty transition frames and a consistently top-heavy layout with a dead lower third, so it needs a revision pass before the brand posts it.

defects: Poster frame is taken mid-transition: the 'Le coupe-chou' headline is cut in half by the reveal mask and the razor is only a small stub, so the thumbnail reads as broken
At 0.4 s the hook line 'c'était quand ?' is still half-masked; the hook is not fully readable in the first half-second

The illustrations are flat and generic (towel stack, brush, razor); the old-school craft of the shave comes through in the type, not in the visuals, and nothing shows the real shop or a person
The price and duration are repeated: '40 MIN · 35 €' on the product slide, then '35 € / 40 minutes' again on its own slide, which adds no new information
'RDV EN LIGNE EN 30 S' is an unverified claim not in the brief, set very small with low contrast
The towel on step 01 appears first as grey placeholder-looking bars before its striped final state
scores.verdict: This is a coherent, well-typeset barber-shop system: serif and condensed pairing, barber-pole edge, red/black/gold palette, a clear 3-step ritual and a complete CTA end card with URL, address and hours in correct French. The poster is caught mid-transition, the hook is still masked at the start, lower-frame space is underused, and the end card resolves late, so it needs a fix pass before posting.

defects: Poster frame is a mid-animation state: title 'Le coupe-chou' is clipped by a reveal mask, with a stray gold dash as the only visual, so the cover looks broken
Hook frame at 0.2s shows only a clipped 'Votre dernier' with the rest of the headline missing; the first second has no strong visual
Several frames sampled at step transitions are near-empty: a plain red frame around 16s (with only a gold strip at the top) and a bare black frame with only a small MC logo at 19.5s
Text sits in the upper half or the middle while large dead areas remain at the bottom of the hook, price and end-card frames; the end card is top-heavy
Very small text: step descriptions, 'DURÉE · 10 MIN' labels, the 'ÉTAPE x/3' tag, the 'NOUVEAU soin' stamp and the address/hours are hard to read on a phone
'RDV EN LIGNE EN 30 S' at the bottom of the end card is almost invisible (dark red on black), and it makes an unsupported claim

The blaireau illustration reads like a microphone or ice-cream cone rather than a shaving brush; the towel stack is generic flat clip-art

scores.verdict: The brand register is coherent (barber-pole stripe, black, red and gold, serif type, good French copy), and the tone suits a neighbourhood old-school barbershop. Execution is weakened by a broken-looking poster and hook frames, empty transition frames, tiny text, top-heavy layouts with empty bottoms, and a weak end card whose secondary line is nearly invisible, so it is not postable as is.

defects: Frame 3: the foam blob covers the 'le blaireau.' title, leaving it half-faded and illegible ('le blaireau' reads as 'le blaireau' behind foam); the brush overlaps the text.
Frames 4-5: the screen is almost entirely foam texture with only a small title in the middle. Large dead areas, weak hierarchy, and no illustration for coupe-chou.
Frame 4 has a stray black sliver/artifact at the left edge and blobby foam edges at the top corners.
The razor/blade sprite in the reveal frame clips the 'à l'ancienne' text and the tagline ('coupe-ch' cut off), and it lands on top of the type mid-transition.
A grey rectangular artifact sits at the left edge of the end card (visible in the poster at y≈830-1215), left over from the razor sprite.
Jagged white tear/scratch slivers cut through the 'rasage / à l'ancienne' title area and the tagline zone, and the 'g' descender is clipped by one. They look like rendering debris rather than design.

The end card leaves the lower third as empty foam. Address, hours and URL are tiny (about 12 px on the sheet, roughly 24 px at full size) and sit in the bottom safe zone, so they are barely legible on a phone.
Proper nouns are lowercase: 'maison castel', 'lyon', 'croix-rousse', 'd'austerlitz'. In French these should be capitalized, and the straight apostrophe in 'd'austerlitz' is not typographic.
The eyebrow 'nouveau chez maison castel' is small and letterspaced, so the brand name is weak and there is no logo or wordmark.
There is no call to action beyond the 'rendez-vous en ligne' label. The end card is static for the last several seconds, and the first frame (towel plus tiny text) is a weak scroll-stopping hook.
Numbering '1/3 2/3 3/3' is very small, and the 3/3 step has no visual.
scores.verdict: The burgundy, cream and gold palette with a high-contrast Didone display face suits an old-school barbershop, and the shaving-foam wipe concept is clever. Execution is undermined by foam covering the titles, near-empty foam frames, a razor sprite clipping the text, a grey edge artifact, tear-shaped debris in the headline, lowercase proper nouns and tiny end-card info, so it is not postable as is.

defects: Weak hook: at 0.4 s the frame is a mostly empty burgundy screen with a half-faded headline and a barely visible '1 / 3'. There is no motion, no image and no question to stop the scroll.
The blaireau beat has a foam blob covering the headline 'le blaireau.' mid-transition, so the text is illegible (sheet frame 3).

The coupe-chou beat is just text on a flat foam texture with no razor illustration, which is inconsistent with the illustrated towel in beat 1. Beats 2 and 3 (sheet frames 4-5) look like empty placeholder screens.
In sheet frame 4, dark ragged blobs from the transition show at the frame edges and the right side is clipped.
In sheet frame 6 the headline 'rasage' sits in a thin band at the top while the rest of the frame is empty foam.
The end card has stray white shard/sliver artifacts cutting across its bands, near 'à l'ancienne', under the list and beside '35 €'. They read as rendering glitches, not intentional razor strokes.
Proper nouns are forced to lowercase ('lyon', 'austerlitz', 'croix-rousse', 'maison castel'), which breaks French typographic conventions for place and brand names.
The end card stays static for roughly the last 40% of the video (sheet frames 8-12 are identical), which is dead time on Reels/TikTok.
The foam zones at the top and bottom of the end card are empty and do nothing.
The CTA 'rendez-vous en ligne' has no imperative verb such as 'Réservez', so it pushes booking weakly.
There are no people, faces or real barbershop atmosphere, so the warm, old-school neighbourhood feel from the brief is barely there.
scores.verdict: The concept holds together: burgundy and cream with a Didone serif gives the right old-school register, the three-step structure works, and the razor wipe that reveals the end card is a nice idea. But the hook is limp, beats 2-3 are empty foam screens with a legibility collision, and the end card has glitchy shards, lowercased proper nouns and a long static hold, so it needs another pass before posting.

defects: The hook is slow and abstract: at 0.5 s the screen shows only 'Une valse' in low-contrast grey-beige on dark green, plus stray staff lines. Nothing about shaving or a barber appears in the first second, so viewers will scroll past.
The product name 'Rasage à l'ancienne' never appears as a headline. It shows up only in a tiny uppercase kicker, so the service being launched is under-sold.
The kicker wraps badly, 'RASAGE À L'ANCIENNE · MAISON' then an orphaned 'CASTEL' on its own line, which splits the brand name.
The hot-towel illustration reads as a mug or a loaf of bread, not a towel. Because the steam lines sit above it, it looks like a hot drink.
The 'Temps 1/2/3' markers are brown ovals that read as coffee beans or footprints. The dance-step idea does not come across.
The bottom 35–40% of the frame is empty on every scene (steps, price, end card), so the layout feels top-heavy. The end card also leaves a large dead zone under the hours.
Transition frames fade to almost nothing. The sheet shows a washed-out grey frame with a ghost '1', and a near-blank beige frame with a faded 'La serviette chaude'.

The staff lines and giant numerals are cropped at the frame edges. The '1', '2' and '3' are cut off on the right, and the staff runs off the left. This looks intentional but gives an unfinished feel on the hook frame.

On the price scene the '40 min' counter spends most of its screen time on partial values (17, 19 min). A viewer who glances briefly may see a wrong duration, and the second row of ticks ends in an odd stub.
No real photos or signs of the shop (Croix-Rousse, the three chairs, a warm atmosphere). The illustrations are generic and could belong to any barber.
'Rendez-vous' is displayed with a Bodoni hyphen so thin it almost disappears at small size.
scores.verdict: The waltz-in-three-beats concept is a smart, distinctive fit for a three-step shave, and the palette and Bodoni typography suit an old-school neighbourhood barber well. But the hook is weak, the lower third is empty throughout, the towel illustration is ambiguous, and the new service's name is buried in a small kicker, so it needs another pass before posting.

defects: Factual error: the price card says '19 min' whereas the brief says the treatment lasts 40 min; the client would not post wrong information

scores.verdict: The waltz-in-three-beats concept (temps 1-2-3 for towel, brush, razor) is a distinctive, coherent idea with a fitting bottle-green, burgundy and cream palette and good display serif typography. It is undermined by a wrong duration (19 min instead of 40), a hook that never says barber, crude razor art overlapping the numeral, tiny secondary text and unbalanced empty lower areas, so it is not postable as is.

scores.verdict: A witty, coherent treasure-map concept that turns the ingredient list into a playful geography and keeps the price and brand clearly present, with good French copy and an authentic vintage look. It is held back by small, crowded map labels that overlap toppings, a slightly unappetizing dark truffle, and no call to action, but it is postable as is.

scores.verdict: A cohesive, on-brand sunrise-over-the-lake system with strong serif/sans typography, clean French copy and a clear per-slide structure (posture, breath, duration) ending on a proper 7h15 / shala-annecy.fr CTA. It is held back by crude stick-figure illustrations that don't always read as the named pose, a cramped and inconsistent final slide, and minor collisions on the cover, so it is good but not best-in-class.

defects: Poster frame is a broken mid-transition state: headline clipped to a sliver of glyph tops, faint eyebrow, otherwise empty. Unusable as thumbnail.

Progress bar at the top may collide with the TikTok/Instagram UI safe zone.

ranks.rationale:
k183 is the most distinctive and best crafted. It works as one idea: an old-style technical engraving, with each sign as a numbered "Fig." showing a cutaway of the water heater and a magnified detail (corroded anode, scale at the bottom of the tank, dripping safety valve, rating plate with the manufacture date circled, scaled-up heating element). Each slide splits into "Le signe" and "À faire", and a footer tracker fills in as you swipe. The serif typography is refined, it signals craft and a family business since 1987, and the CTA (49 €, "offert si remplacement", 3 générations, 9 techniciens, 7j/7, phone number, website) is complete. It covers the whole brief and reads well at 1080x1350.

k154 is the strongest of the navy/copper "clean flat" group. Its diagrams are really educational: labelled Anode, Résistance, Calcaire, Molette and Évacuation, a plate reading "Fab. 03/2013" next to an age gauge, and a chart linking millimetres of scale to extra consumption. Each slide has a severity marker ("À traiter vite", "À surveiller"), and the offer slide is clear, with what the diagnostic covers.

k112 is close behind. The cover is strong, with chips for the 5 signs. Illustrations are good (tap and thermometer, a "CLAC!" tank, gouttes = OK vs filet = alerte), each slide has clear "Pourquoi / Quoi faire" cards, sign 4 uses a big "10+ ans" treatment, and the CTA has trust stats. It feels slightly more generic than k154.

k156 is very similar and polished: an annotated cover, a Normal / Pas normal split on sign 3, and a lifespan bar. Its outlined numbers and the familiar template put it a bit below the two above.

k105 is solid and punchy, with a navy/red/mustard palette, "TOC TOC BLOUB" and a "+30 %" chart. Its icons are cruder and the all-caps heavy type is less refined.

k128 is clean and readable in condensed caps with orange accents. The illustrations are simple (glass of rusty water, calendar showing "10+"), which makes it competent but generic.

k109 puts signs 4 and 5 on a single cramped slide to make room for two offer and contact slides. That breaks the one-sign-per-slide rhythm. Its illustrations are minimal (a drop, a sound icon).

k134 comes last. The pressure-gauge concept is clever, but it repeats the same gauge on all 7 slides, so the visuals barely change. The "À faire" advice is thin ("Demandez un diagnostic"), and the cover has visible defects: the circumflex on "LÂCHER" collides with the line above it, and the needle runs over the numeral 5.

What separates the top from the bottom: the top pieces have an illustration made for each sign that actually teaches something and fits the brand story, while the bottom ones rely on a generic template, repeat visuals, compress content, or show typographic collisions.

I judged only the contact sheets. All eight pieces have French copy, a 4:5 layout, the -38 % and 11-day claims, and the 14-day trial CTA with ledgerly.io. What separates them is how well they tell the story, how polished they look and whether any frame is broken.

k165 is first. It tells the clearest story: one overdue invoice (23 days, 13 200 €), then per-client tone and timing chips across three clients, then a tone slider with a best-time picker, the proof on a bold green field, and a CTA that sums up the benefit ("L'IA relance. Vous encaissez."). The type is confident, the colour change from cream to navy to green has rhythm, and no frame is broken.

k175 is a close second. Its hook is a receivables total that climbs from 33 962 € to 38 420 €, which a CFO will recognise. It shows the AI plan per client and an SMS being sent and marked paid. It is the only piece with a DSO curve (52 days down to 41). It loses a little for one half-wiped transition frame and a CTA end card that feels generic.

k147 is third. It has the most refined editorial style: a serif-italic accent, invoice slips stamped "IMPAYÉE", a believable app UI with a message being written, and a before/after bar chart for DSO. One frame is fully blank.

k177 is fourth. It has a distinctive dark "music track" idea where the tone and send time pick a note, and personalised messages are revealed word by word. It looks premium and has a clear timecode, but the metaphor is harder to read at a glance, and the dim text in the hook frames lowers legibility.

k113 is fifth. It is solid and covers everything: a bold "36 → 47 jours de retard" hook, a dashboard with the best-time card, and a sequenced timeline of reminders. It is clean but more predictable, and one frame is empty.

k198 is sixth. Its "vending machine" grid of tone and timing is original and memorable, but it is hard to understand without explanation. The palette is heavy, and the end card relies on the URL pill without much tie back to the product.

k169 is seventh. It is competent but generic: dark cards, tone chips and a slider, with no strong hook image. It also has an empty frame and a faded CTA frame.

k108 is last. The graph-paper idea and the per-client payment timelines are smart. However, it shows clear rendering defects: a huge green circle covering the content, text cropped at the left edge, a blank logo frame, and the DSO line cut off at the bottom of the frame. It also shows "10 jours" (the counter mid-count) where the brief says 11. These errors outweigh its good idea.

I judged each piece from its sheet.jpg and poster.jpg against the brief: a 9:16 Reel in French for the new 35 € / 40 min "Rasage à l'ancienne" (hot towel, shaving brush, straight razor), aimed at pushing online booking, with the address and opening hours included.

1. k184 is the most polished and on-brand. The warm old-school dark and gold look fits the brief. The hook ("Posez le rasoir jetable. Et offrez-vous 40 minutes") is strong. The line icons of the three steps are clean and consistent. Price and duration are clear. The end card has the MC seal, the booking button for maisoncastel.fr, the address and the hours. Nothing is wrong or missing.

2. k151 has a witty hook ("On ne se rase pas. On se fait raser.") and the barber pole. The step medallions are elegant and the ending is complete: 35 € / 40 min, the seal, "Réservez votre fauteuil", the website, address and hours. It adds a fourth step (a soothing balm) that the brief doesn't mention. A few frames catch text half-way through a mask reveal.

3. k174 has the most original idea: shaving foam wipes across the screen and becomes the transition. Its deep burgundy and cream typography feel artisanal. The end card holds every piece of information. However, the opening frames are sparse, several frames are almost empty foam, and the last half of the video sits on the same static card.

4. k120 has lively barber-stripe borders and a punchy hook ("Ton dernier vrai rasage, c'était quand ?"). The pacing is colourful, with a strong 35 € card and a complete end card. The informal "tu" is acceptable for this audience. The straight-razor illustration is clumsy, one frame is blank, and the small info text is faint.

5. k110 uses the same hook and a similar structure to k120. The editorial layout is good and the end card is complete. It has more empty or transitional frames (a plain red flat frame, a partial razor), and one frame catches the text mid-animation.

6. k107 has a clever idea: a 40-minute clock dial that fills step by step, and its ending is premium. But the hero object in the hook ("On a ressorti le coupe-chou") is drawn as a serrated table knife rather than a straight razor, which is a visible mistake for a barber. It also has several blank or transitional frames.

7. k142 is correct and complete: barber pole, "Et si vous preniez 40 min", a card per step, 35 €, and a red booking button. But it is visually monotonous: the same brown background throughout, several fully empty frames, and small boxed step cards that read poorly on a phone.

8. k190 has an appealing waltz-in-three-beats concept and a good palette. However, its price card says "19 min", which contradicts the brief's 40 minutes, and the 40-minute duration never appears anywhere else. It also has washed-out transition frames.

What separates top from bottom: the top three combine a clear hook, a coherent premium old-school look and a complete, legible booking end card. The bottom candidates lose points for factual or visual mistakes (k190's wrong duration, k107's knife in place of a straight razor) or for flat, empty pacing (k142).
